answer: An attacker must acquire and bond many distinct devices, making forgery costlier than legitimate participation. Sybil resistance can work through a proof-of-stake bond tied to a unique hardware root of trust: each agent must lock tokens behind a verifiable identity, and a challenge period lets peers slash the bond if duplicates appear. This creates a bridge between identity and capital, so reaching the summit of influence requires real stake, while honest agents navigate a wide ocean of low-cost transactions safely. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
